chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed Asma bint Umays gave birth to Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered her, when she intended to enter the state of Ihram from Dhi al-Hulayfah, to place cotton and cloth [for absorption] and to proclaim the Talbiyah for Hajj.

So when they arrived in Mecca and performed the rituals, and eighteen days had passed for her, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered her to perform Tawaf around the House and pray, although the bleeding had not ceased, so she did so.

key_terms.تَحْتَشِيَ: to place/insert for absorption (referring to using cotton/cloth for bleeding)
key_terms.تُهِلَّ: to proclaim the Talbiyah (invocation for Hajj)
key_terms.ذِي الْحُلَيْفَةِ: Dhi al-Hulayfah (a specific Miqat station near Mecca)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman who gives birth during Hajj regarding Ihram and Tawaf while in postpartum bleeding?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the juristic principle that postpartum bleeding (nifas) does not invalidate the essential pillars of Hajj, specifically Tawaf and Salat, as demonstrated by the Prophet’s directive to Asma bint Umays. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that while bleeding necessitates specific accommodations (such as using cotton/cloth for purity), it does not require delaying the core rituals, thereby distinguishing between conditions that break Ihram and those that merely modify ritual purity practices.
